subproblem.title: Basic properties of the weight measure θHᵏ⌞M of an IMRep: absolute continuity both ways, formula on Borel sets, local finiteness, and R.action ω = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^P (no openness is assumed) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in W (IMRep W k): M = R.carrier is a Borel set with M ⊆ W, θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable with θ(x) ≥ 1 for x ∈ M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W, and ξ = R.orient : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M; here Hᵏ = μHE[k], R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ (the weight θHᵏ⌞M, contract IMRep.measure) and R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) (contract IMRep.action). Then: (a) R.measure ≪ Hᵏ⌞M; (b) Hᵏ⌞M ≪ R.measure; (c) R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ (lower Lebesgue integral of the [0,∞]-valued cast of θ) for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P; (d) R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0; (e) R.measure(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W; (f) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for R.measure; (g) for every k-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) (an arbitrary DifferentialForm; no smoothness or integrability is assumed), R.action ω = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep W k), R.measure ≪ μHE[k].restrict R.carrier ∧ μHE[k].restrict R.carrier ≪ R.measure ∧ (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∫⁻ x in R.carrier ∩ A, (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[k]) ∧ R.measure R.carrierᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → R.measure K < ∞) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable R.orient R.measure ∧ ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k, R.action ω = ∫ x, R.orient x (ω x) ∂R.measure
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the identities R.measure = θHᵏ⌞M and 'R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure (integral against a measure with density)' stated in the preamble of the selected node's proof and used in its steps 5–9. They are needed by the selected node itself (steps 5 and 6: finiteness of R_x.measure on compact sets, measurability of ξ_x for R_x.measure, transport of (IMC)(d), and R_x.action(ω) = ∫ ξ_x(ω) dR_x.measure) and by the sibling glue (steps 7–9).
Notation: ν := Hᵏ⌞M = μHE[k].restrict M and g(x) := θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞], so that R.measure = ν.withDensity g by the definition IMRep.measure.
1. g is measurable: θ is measurable (field measurable_mult of R), and the cast ℕ → [0, ∞] is measurable because every map out of ℕ is.
2. Proof of (c). Let A be Borel. By the definition of a measure with density, R.measure(A) = ∫_A g dν = ∫ g d(ν⌞A) (Mathlib withDensity_apply, A measurable). Since A is measurable, ν⌞A = (Hᵏ⌞M)⌞A = Hᵏ⌞(A ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ.
3. Proof of (d). ℝ^P ∖ M is Borel because M is (field measurableSet_carrier). By (c), R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = ∫_{M ∩ (ℝ^P∖M)} θ dHᵏ = ∫_∅ θ dHᵏ = 0.
4. Proof of (e). Let K ⊆ W be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so by (c) R.measure(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ, and this is finite by the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R applied to the compact set K ⊆ W.
5. Proof of (a). Let A ⊆ ℝ^P with ν(A) = 0, and choose a Borel set A' ⊇ A with ν(A') = 0 (a measurable hull). Then ν⌞A' is the zero measure, so R.measure(A') = ∫_{A'} g dν = 0, and R.measure(A) ≤ R.measure(A') = 0. Hence R.measure ≪ ν (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous).
6. Proof of (b). First, g(x) ≠ 0 for ν-a.e. x: ν-a.e. x lies in M (ν(ℝ^P ∖ M) = Hᵏ((ℝ^P ∖ M) ∩ M) = Hᵏ(∅) = 0; Mathlib ae_restrict_mem, M Borel), and for x ∈ M, g(x) = θ(x) ≥ 1 (field mult_pos). Now let R.measure(A) = 0 and choose a Borel set A' ⊇ A with R.measure(A') = 0 (a measurable hull). Then ∫_{A'} g dν = 0, so g = 0 holds (ν⌞A')-a.e. (Mathlib lintegral_eq_zero_iff, g measurable). Together with g ≠ 0 ν-a.e. this gives (ν⌞A')(ℝ^P) = 0, i.e. ν(A') = 0, hence ν(A) = 0. So ν ≪ R.measure (this is Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous', whose hypotheses are exactly that g is a.e. measurable and g ≠ 0 ν-a.e.).
7. Proof of (f). ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient). By (a), R.measure ≪ ν, and a.e. strong measurability passes to absolutely continuous measures (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac). Hence ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for R.measure.
8. Proof of (g). Let ω be any k-form and h(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)) ∈ ℝ. Put f(x) := (θ(x) : ℝ≥0), a measurable ℝ≥0-valued function whose cast to [0, ∞] is g, so R.measure = ν.withDensity (x ↦ (f(x) : [0,∞])). By Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul (for a measurable ℝ≥0-valued density f and an arbitrary function h, ∫ h d(ν.withDensity f) = ∫ f • h dν; no integrability assumption is needed, because h is integrable for ν.withDensity f exactly when f·h is integrable for ν, and both Bochner integrals are 0 otherwise), ∫ h dR.measure = ∫ f(x)·h(x) dν(x) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x), using f(x) • h(x) = (θ(x) : ℝ)·h(x). The right-hand side is R.action ω by the definition IMRep.action. ∎
proof_key_steps: R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ with θ measurable; withDensity_apply and restrict_restrict give R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ for Borel A, hence R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 and, by local integrability of θ, R.measure(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ W.
A measure with density is absolutely continuous with respect to its base measure; conversely θ ≥ 1 on M makes the density a.e. nonzero, so Hᵏ⌞M ≪ R.measure.
A.e. strong measurability of ξ passes from Hᵏ⌞M to R.measure by absolute continuity.
integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul turns ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure into ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = R.action ω for every form ω.

subproblem.title: Gluing: a current with a mass representation that agrees locally with integer multiplicity representations is integer multiplicity (IM is local)
subproblem.statement: Assume (IMC)(a), passed as a hypothesis: the exact first conjunct of the frozen statement of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (hypothesis (IMC) of the selected node), namely: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and all Borel sets M ⊆ M' ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x iff it is one of M' at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt). Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k), μ a Borel measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k) such that μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Suppose every x ∈ U lies in an open set W ⊆ U on which there is an IMRep R in W (IMRep W k) with μ⌞W = R.measure (the weight θ_R Hᵏ⌞M_R) and ξ(y) = R.orient(y) for μ-a.e. y ∈ W. Then X is integer multiplicity in U (IsIntegerMultiplicity X).

Source: steps 7–9 of the selected node's proof (the gluing in Part I, T4 of the grandparent proof; Simon 6.3.1, chapter-06.txt lines 733–753, and the localization remark 8.3(1), lines 2311–2317). The selected proof equips the glued carrier with the local orientations ξ_{x_i}; since the hypotheses give ξ = ξ_{x_i} a.e. on each piece, we use ξ itself as the glued orientation, which reduces the representation step to an identity of measures. Uses the sibling imrep_measure. Notation: Hᵏ := μHE[k]; for an IMRep R write M_R, θ_R, ξ_R for R.carrier, R.mult, R.orient. By imrep_measure, for every IMRep R (in any set): (b) Hᵏ⌞M_R ≪ R.measure; (c) R.measure(A) = ∫_{M_R∩A} θ_R dHᵏ for every Borel A; (g) R.action ω = ∫ ξ_R(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x) for every k-form ω.
1. The case U = ∅. Then μ(ℝ^P) = μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, so X(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ = 0 for every ω. The IMRep in U with carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents X: ∅ is Borel, ∅ ⊆ U, ∅ is countably k-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero), the multiplicity is measurable, the positivity condition is vacuous, every integral over ∅ is 0 (this gives local integrability and action 0 = X(ω)), and Hᵏ⌞∅ = 0, so the measurability and orientation conditions hold trivially. From now on U ≠ ∅.
2. Countable subcover. For each x ∈ U choose an open W_x ⊆ U with x ∈ W_x and an IMRep R_x in W_x as in the hypothesis. The open sets W_x (x ∈ U) cover U and ℝ^P is second countable, so there is a countable set T ⊆ U with ⋃_{x∈T} W_x = ⋃_{x∈U} W_x = U (Lindelöf; Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). T ≠ ∅ because U ≠ ∅, so T = {x_0, x_1, x_2, …} for a sequence (x_i)_{i∈ℕ} (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range; repetitions allowed). Write W_i := W_{x_i}, R_i := R_{x_i}, and M_i, θ_i, ξ_i for the carrier, multiplicity and orientation of R_i. Then each W_i is open, W_i ⊆ U, ⋃_i W_i = U, M_i ⊆ W_i, μ⌞W_i = R_i.measure, and ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) for μ-a.e. y ∈ W_i.
3. Disjoint pieces. Put A_i := W_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} W_j (Mathlib disjointed). The A_i are Borel, pairwise disjoint, A_i ⊆ W_i, and ⋃_i A_i = ⋃_i W_i = U.
4. Glued data. Let M := ⋃_i (M_i ∩ A_i) and define θ : ℝ^P → ℕ by θ(y) := θ_i(y) if y ∈ A_i (the index i is unique) and θ(y) := 0 if y ∉ U (for instance θ(y) := θ_{n(y)}(y) with n(y) the least n such that y ∈ A_n, Nat.find, and θ(y) := 0 if there is no such n). Then: (i) M is Borel and M ⊆ U (M_i ⊆ W_i ⊆ U); since the A_i are pairwise disjoint, M ∩ A_i = M_i ∩ A_i for every i. (ii) θ is measurable: it takes values in the countable set ℕ, and for every m ∈ ℕ, θ⁻¹({m}) = ⋃_i (A_i ∩ θ_i⁻¹({m})) ∪ E_m with E_m := ℝ^P ∖ U if m = 0 and E_m := ∅ otherwise, a countable union of Borel sets (Mathlib measurable_to_countable'). (iii) θ = θ_i on A_i; in particular θ(y) = θ_i(y) ≥ 1 for y ∈ M_i ∩ A_i, so θ ≥ 1 on M. (iv) M is countably k-rectifiable: each M_i ∩ A_i ⊆ M_i is (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono), and so is the countable union (countablyRectifiable_iUnion).
5. The measure identity μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ. Let S be Borel. The sets S ∩ A_i are Borel and pairwise disjoint with union S ∩ U, and μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0. Since S ∩ A_i ⊆ W_i and μ⌞W_i = R_i.measure, μ(S ∩ A_i) = μ(S ∩ A_i ∩ W_i) = R_i.measure(S ∩ A_i). Using imrep_measure (c) for R_i, then (i) and (iii): μ(S) = μ(S ∩ U) = Σ_i μ(S ∩ A_i) = Σ_i R_i.measure(S ∩ A_i) = Σ_i ∫_{M_i ∩ S ∩ A_i} θ_i dHᵏ = Σ_i ∫_{M ∩ S ∩ A_i} θ dHᵏ = ∫_{M∩S} θ dHᵏ, the last step by countable additivity of the lower integral over the pairwise disjoint Borel sets M ∩ S ∩ A_i, whose union is M ∩ S because M ⊆ U = ⋃_i A_i (Mathlib lintegral_iUnion). Finally ∫_{M∩S} θ dHᵏ = ((Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ)(S) (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). Two measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal, so μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ.
6. Consequences. (a) For compact K ⊆ U (closed, hence Borel), ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ = μ(K) < ∞ by step 5. (b) Since θ ≥ 1 on M, Hᵏ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. (c) θ ≠ 0 holds Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. (θ ≥ 1 on M, and Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. point lies in the Borel set M), so Hᵏ⌞M ≪ (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ = μ (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous'). (d) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac with (c)).
7. Orientation. Fix i and put N_i := M_i ∩ A_i = M ∩ A_i (Borel). (α) By the field orients of R_i, for Hᵏ⌞M_i-a.e. y there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_i y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_i(y)) Q; since N_i ⊆ M_i this holds for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). (β) By hypothesis ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) for μ-a.e. y ∈ W_i, i.e. for (μ⌞W_i)-a.e. y (ae_restrict_iff', W_i Borel), i.e. for R_i.measure-a.e. y. By imrep_measure (b), Hᵏ⌞M_i ≪ R_i.measure, so ξ = ξ_i holds Hᵏ⌞M_i-a.e., hence Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. (γ) Apply (IMC)(a) in the open set W_i to the Borel sets N_i ⊆ M_i ⊆ W_i. Its local finiteness hypothesis holds: for compact K ⊆ W_i, Hᵏ(M_i ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M_i∩K} θ_i dHᵏ < ∞, because θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i and R_i is locally integrable in W_i (field locallyIntegrable_mult). So for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k N_i y Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_i y Q. (δ) Apply (IMC)(a) in the open set U to the Borel sets N_i ⊆ M ⊆ U, with local finiteness from 6(b): for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k N_i y Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M y Q. Intersecting these four full-measure sets: for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y, the subspace Q from (α) is an approximate tangent space of N_i at y by (γ), hence of M at y by (δ), and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q holds because ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) by (β). Since M = ⋃_i N_i is a countable union, the property 'there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q' holds for Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. y (Mathlib ae_restrict_iUnion_iff).
8. The glued IMRep. R := (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U: measurableSet_carrier and carrier_subset by 4(i), rectifiable by 4(iv), measurable_mult by 4(ii), mult_pos by 4(iii), locallyIntegrable_mult by 6(a), aestronglyMeasurable_orient by 6(d), and orients by step 7. By definition R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ, which equals μ by step 5.
9. Representation. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), imrep_measure (g) applied to R gives R.action ω = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) = X(ω). So R represents X, and X is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: If U = ∅ then μ = 0 and the empty IMRep represents X.
Choose the local data (W_x, R_x); by Lindelöf take a countable subcover (W_i) and the disjoint Borel pieces A_i := W_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} W_j, which cover U.
Glue M := ⋃_i (M_i ∩ A_i) and θ := θ_i on A_i (0 off U): M is Borel and countably k-rectifiable, θ is measurable and θ ≥ 1 on M.
μ⌞W_i = R_i.measure, imrep_measure (c) and countable additivity give μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ; hence local integrability of θ and Hᵏ⌞M ≪ μ, so ξ is Hᵏ⌞M-measurable.
Take ξ as glued orientation: ξ = ξ_i Hᵏ-a.e. on M_i ∩ A_i (imrep_measure (b)), and (IMC)(a) in W_i and in U shows that the approximate tangent spaces of M_i, M_i ∩ A_i and M agree a.e. there.
R.action ω = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ = X(ω) by imrep_measure (g), so X is integer multiplicity.

subproblem.title: Equal set integrals against all test forms of an open set B determine the orientation a.e. on B
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, B ⊆ ℝ^P open, μ₁, μ₂ Borel measures on ℝ^P, and ξ₁, ξ₂ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k: continuous linear functionals on the space Λ^k = Covector (Euclid P) k of k-covectors). Assume: (i) μ₁(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ B; (ii) μ₁⌞B = μ₂⌞B; (iii) ξ_i is a.e. strongly measurable for μ_i (i = 1, 2); (iv) for i = 1, 2, for μ_i-a.e. x and every α ∈ Λ^k, |ξ_i(x)(α)| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm); (v) ∫_E ξ₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁(x) = ∫_E ξ₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂(x) for every Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^P and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^k(B) (TestFormOn B k: smooth compactly supported k-forms on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ B). Then ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x) for μ₁-a.e. x ∈ B, i.e. for μ₁-a.e. x, x ∈ B implies ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (B : Set (Euclid P)) (μ₁ μ₂ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ₁ ξ₂ : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), IsOpen B → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ B → μ₁ K < ∞) → μ₁.restrict B = μ₂.restrict B → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ₁ μ₁ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ₂ μ₂ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ₁, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ₁ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ₂, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ₂ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn B k), MeasurableSet E → ∫ x in E, ξ₁ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₁ = ∫ x in E, ξ₂ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₂) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ₁, x ∈ B → ξ₁ x = ξ₂ x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the selected node's proof, after the application of the sibling theorem cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq, which the selected node performs itself and which yields hypothesis (v) with μ₁ = μ_X, ξ₁ = ξ_X, μ₂ = R_x.measure, ξ₂ = ξ_x: 'For a k-covector α, a compact K ⊆ B' and φ ∈ C_c^∞(B') with φ = 1 on K, taking ω := φα and E ⊆ K gives ∫_E (ξ_X(α) − ξ_x(α)) dν = 0 for all Borel E ⊆ K, so ξ_X(y)(α) = ξ_x(y)(α) for ν-a.e. y ∈ K. Exhausting B' by countably many compact sets and letting α run through a finite basis of k-covectors: ξ_X = ξ_x μ_X-a.e. on B''. Uses the sibling covector_fd.
Notation: ν := μ₁⌞B, which equals μ₂⌞B by (ii). For α ∈ Λ^k and i = 1, 2 put f_i^α(x) := ξ_i(x)(α) ∈ ℝ.
1. Restrictions. For every Borel E ⊆ B, μ₁⌞E = (μ₁⌞B)⌞E = ν⌞E and μ₂⌞E = (μ₂⌞B)⌞E = ν⌞E (Mathlib Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset). For compact K ⊆ B, ν(K) = μ₁(K ∩ B) = μ₁(K) < ∞ by (i).
2. Measurability and bounds under ν. ν = μ₁⌞B ≤ μ₁ and ν = μ₂⌞B ≤ μ₂, so by (iii) ξ₁ and ξ₂ are a.e. strongly measurable for ν, and by (iv) |ξ_i(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for ν-a.e. x and every α (ae_restrict_of_ae). For fixed α the evaluation map Λ_k → ℝ, ζ ↦ ζ(α), is continuous and linear, so f_i^α is a.e. strongly measurable for ν and |f_i^α| ≤ |α| holds ν-a.e. Consequently f_i^α is ν-integrable on every compact K ⊆ B, being a.e. bounded on a set of finite ν-measure (step 1; Mathlib Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded).
3. Cut-off. Fix α ∈ Λ^k and a compact K ⊆ B. Since K is compact and B is open, there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ B (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open), and cthickening δ K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper). The open set V := thickening δ K contains K, so the smooth Urysohn lemma (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff for the open set V and the closed set K ⊆ V) gives a C^∞ function φ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with support φ = V and φ(y) = 1 for y ∈ K. Then tsupport φ = closure V ⊆ cthickening δ K ⊆ B, and tsupport φ is compact.
4. Test form. Let ω(y) := φ(y)·α, a constant covector multiplied by φ. It is C^∞ (product of a smooth function with a constant), its support is contained in support φ, so it has compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ B. Hence ω ∈ 𝒟^k(B), and ω(y) = α for every y ∈ K.
5. Set integrals over Borel subsets of K. Let E ⊆ K be Borel. For y ∈ E, ξ_i(y)(ω(y)) = ξ_i(y)(α) = f_i^α(y), so the set integrals over E of ξ_i(ω) and of f_i^α coincide (setIntegral_congr_fun, E measurable). Using (v) and step 1 (E ⊆ K ⊆ B): ∫_E f₁^α dν = ∫_E f₁^α dμ₁ = ∫_E ξ₁(ω) dμ₁ = ∫_E ξ₂(ω) dμ₂ = ∫_E f₂^α dμ₂ = ∫_E f₂^α dν.
6. Equality a.e. on K. Let ν_K := ν⌞K, a finite measure by step 1. For every Borel s ⊆ ℝ^P, ν_K⌞s = ν⌞(s ∩ K) (Measure.restrict_restrict), and s ∩ K is a Borel subset of K, so by step 5, ∫_s f₁^α dν_K = ∫_{s∩K} f₁^α dν = ∫_{s∩K} f₂^α dν = ∫_s f₂^α dν_K. Both functions are ν_K-integrable on every s (step 2). By uniqueness of densities (Mathlib ae_eq_of_forall_setIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite, applied to the finite measure ν_K), f₁^α = f₂^α holds ν_K-a.e.; that is, ξ₁(y)(α) = ξ₂(y)(α) for ν-a.e. y ∈ K (ae_restrict_iff', K Borel).
7. Exhaustion of B. For j ∈ ℕ let K_j := B̄_j(0) ∖ T_j, where B̄_j(0) is the closed ball of radius j about 0 and T_j := {y : dist(y, z) < 1/(j+1) for some z ∈ ℝ^P ∖ B} is the open 1/(j+1)-neighbourhood of ℝ^P ∖ B (Mathlib thickening; T_j = ∅ if B = ℝ^P). Each K_j is a closed subset of a compact ball, hence compact; K_j ⊆ B, because every point of ℝ^P ∖ B lies in T_j; and ⋃_j K_j = B: a point y ∈ B is not in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ B, which is the intersection of its open δ-neighbourhoods (δ > 0), so y is outside the δ-neighbourhood for some δ > 0, and then y ∈ K_j for every j with j ≥ |y| and 1/(j+1) ≤ δ. Applying step 6 to every K_j and intersecting countably many full-measure sets (ae_all_iff): for ν-a.e. y, for every j, y ∈ K_j implies ξ₁(y)(α) = ξ₂(y)(α). Moreover ν(ℝ^P ∖ B) = 0, so ν-a.e. y lies in B and hence in some K_j. Therefore ξ₁(y)(α) = ξ₂(y)(α) for ν-a.e. y, for each fixed α ∈ Λ^k.
8. Finite basis. By the sibling covector_fd, Λ^k = Covector (Euclid P) k is finite-dimensional; let (b_m)_{m ∈ I}, I finite, be a basis (Module.finBasis). Applying step 7 to each α = b_m and intersecting finitely many full-measure sets: for ν-a.e. y, ξ₁(y)(b_m) = ξ₂(y)(b_m) for all m ∈ I. For such y the linear maps ξ₁(y), ξ₂(y) : Λ^k → ℝ agree on a basis, hence are equal (Module.Basis.ext; a continuous linear map is determined by its underlying linear map, ContinuousLinearMap.coe_injective). So ξ₁ = ξ₂ holds ν-a.e.
9. Conclusion. ν = μ₁⌞B and B is open, hence Borel, so 'ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x) for ν-a.e. x' is equivalent to 'for μ₁-a.e. x, x ∈ B implies ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x)' (Mathlib ae_restrict_iff'). ∎
proof_key_steps: Put ν := μ₁⌞B = μ₂⌞B; a.e. strong measurability and the bound |ξ_i(·)(α)| ≤ |α| pass to ν, and ν is finite on compact subsets of B.

For a covector α and a compact K ⊆ B, a smooth cut-off φ equal to 1 on K with compact support in B gives the test form ω = φα, so hypothesis (v) yields ∫_E ξ₁(α) dν = ∫_E ξ₂(α) dν for every Borel E ⊆ K.
Uniqueness of densities for the finite measure ν⌞K gives ξ₁(α) = ξ₂(α) ν-a.e. on K; a countable compact exhaustion of B extends this to ν-a.e.
Testing on a finite basis of the finite-dimensional covector space (covector_fd) gives ξ₁ = ξ₂ ν-a.e., i.e. μ₁-a.e. on B.

audit.reason: On each compact subset, the common restricted measure is finite and scalar evaluations are integrable. Smooth cutoffs yield all required set-integral equalities; density uniqueness, countable compact exhaustion, and the declared covector_fd dependency give equality of multivectors almost everywhere on B. The final conditional a.e. formulation matches the Lean type exactly.
